title: Distribution Matching Distillation without Fake Score Network
claim: The prior approach needs an extra trained auxiliary network to estimate a score; ours replaces it with a frozen generator-induced surrogate.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels, left-to-right flow, gray vs green headers
description: Two side-by-side rounded panels. The left panel, titled DMD2 under a gray header, shows a block diagram. Data and a red-outlined Generator (Training, flame icon) feed a red Fake-score Network (Training) and a frozen Teacher Network (snowflake icon). The Fake-score Network also feeds a Discriminator that produces a GAN Loss. Fake-score Network and Teacher outputs meet at a red minus circle that gives the DMD Loss, and a Diffusion Loss box sits alongside. The right panel, titled FSF-DMD (Ours) under a green header, is simpler. The Generator feeds a frozen Surrogate Velocity block and the frozen Teacher Network. Their outputs meet at a minus circle that gives the FSF-DMD Loss, and a Consistency Loss branches off the Generator along the top. Red marks trainable parts and blue marks frozen parts. The eye goes first to the two headers, then to the red fake-score network that the right panel removes.
caption: Comparison between DMD2 and FSF-DMD. (Left) DMD2 computes the discrepancy between the teacher and fake scores of the generated samples. It requires an additional network to estimate the fake score, introducing overhead through a separate training loop. (Right) For flow-map generators, FSF-DMD replaces the fake-side estimator with the generator-induced surrogate in [ref], avoiding the additional fake-velocity network and secondary training loop.
abstract: Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) provides an effective distribution-level correction for few-step generation, while relying on an auxiliary fake-score network to track the evolving generative distribution. Recent work combines DMD with a flow-map objective to exploit the benefits of both methods: mode-seeking and mode-covering behaviors. Since this fake-score network increases memory and update overhead, we study whether this explicit tracker can be avoided when the generator has a flow-map structure. In this work, we propose Fake-Score-network-Free DMD (FSF-DMD), a DMD-style correction for flow-map generators, replacing the auxiliary fake-score estimator with a generator-induced surrogate. We observe that this surrogate can be derived from the definition of the fake velocity under a certain perturbation assumption. Building on this insight, we derive a DMD-style objective without a fake-side network, extend it to backward simulation for flow maps, and to a self-teacher variant for training from scratch. In our ImageNet-1K $256\times 256$ experiments, FSF-DMD is competitive with the studied DMD baselines when initialized from pretrained networks and when trained from scratch.
